_meta.title: Phase E - Hardened Policy Examples
_meta.author: Titilayo Yusuf
_meta.note: Three hardening themes corresponding to the root causes found in flaws.cloud Levels 1, 2, 3/4, 5, and 6. Each example pairs the vulnerable pattern observed in the challenge with a hardened replacement. Validate with: aws accessanalyzer validate-policy --policy-type RESOURCE_POLICY --locale EN --policy-document file://<policy>.json --region us-west-2 --profile flaws-sandbox (use --policy-type IDENTITY_POLICY for the IAM role policy). Cross-check identity policies in IAM Policy Simulator in the sandbox account.

theme_1_restrictive_s3_access.description: Hardens the Level 1/2 weaknesses: anonymous ListBucket and the overly broad AuthenticatedUsers grantee.
hardening_notes: Public read is scoped to a named object prefix (public-site/*) only, never the whole bucket, and never s3:ListBucket.
Principal is a specific account ID rather than '*' or any AuthenticatedUsers equivalent; the AuthenticatedUsers S3 canned ACL/grantee itself should never be used.
S3 Block Public Access should additionally be enabled at the account level as a backstop even if a bucket policy is later misconfigured.
Validate with: aws accessanalyzer validate-policy --policy-type RESOURCE_POLICY --locale EN --policy-document file://hardened_bucket_policy.json --region us-west-2 --profile flaws-sandbox

theme_2_credential_secret_handling.description: Hardens the Level 3/4 weaknesses: a long-lived access key committed to source control (and later in Git history) and a plaintext password left in a setup script on an EBS volume.

vulnerable_pattern_observed.example_file: access_keys.txt (committed to Git, later 'deleted' but recoverable from history)

hardened_secrets_manager_reference.description: Application code references a Secrets Manager ARN at runtime instead of embedding any key material in source, scripts, or EC2 user-data.
hardened_secrets_manager_reference.setup_script_equivalent: htpasswd -b /etc/nginx/.htpasswd flaws "$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id app/nginx-basic-auth --query SecretString --output text --region us-west-2)"

hardening_notes: No access key, secret key, or plaintext password is ever written to a file, script, or Git-tracked repository; secrets are fetched at runtime from AWS Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store with SecureString) under a scoped IAM policy.
Pre-commit and pre-deploy secret scanning (e.g. Gitleaks, TruffleHog) should block any commit containing key-like patterns before it reaches a public bucket or repository.

Any credential confirmed or suspected leaked must be deactivated/rotated immediately via 'aws iam update-access-key --status Inactive' followed by deletion, not just removed from the file in a later commit.

Validate the IAM policy with: aws accessanalyzer validate-policy --policy-type IDENTITY_POLICY --locale EN --policy-document file://hardened_secrets_manager_reference_policy.json --region us-west-2 --profile flaws-sandbox

theme_3_ebs_snapshot_sharing.description: Hardens the Level 4 weakness: an EBS snapshot shared publicly, exposing the full filesystem of a decommissioned EC2.

hardened_sharing_pattern.notes: Share explicitly with named account IDs (UserIds) only; never use GroupNames: ['all'].

hardened_scp_or_config_rule.description: Preventive guardrail: an AWS Config managed rule or SCP that flags/denies any snapshot or AMI made public.
hardened_scp_or_config_rule.config_rule: ec2-ebs-encryption-by-default (combined with a custom Config rule or EventBridge+Lambda auto-remediation watching for ModifySnapshotAttribute/ModifyImageAttribute with Group=all)

hardening_notes: Enable EBS encryption by default (ec2 enable-ebs-encryption-by-default) in every region used, so even an accidentally public snapshot cannot be read without the account's KMS key.
Enable the account-level EBS snapshot block public access setting: aws ec2 enable-snapshot-block-public-access --state block-all-sharing --region us-west-2 --profile flaws-sandbox.

Periodically audit snapshot permissions with: aws ec2 describe-snapshots --owner-ids self --region us-west-2 --profile flaws-sandbox, then aws ec2 describe-snapshot-attribute --snapshot-id <id> --attribute createVolumePermission for each, checking for Group: all.

bonus_theme_ec2_imdsv2_and_least_privile.description: Hardens the Level 5 weakness: SSRF against IMDSv1 exposing instance role credentials, and an overly broad instance role.

hardened_metadata_options.cli_example: aws ec2 modify-instance-metadata-options --instance-id i-EXAMPLE00000000 --http-tokens required --http-put-response-hop-limit 1 --region us-west-2 --profile flaws-sandbox

hardening_notes: HttpTokens: required enforces IMDSv2 so a simple GET-based SSRF proxy cannot complete the PUT-token handshake and is refused.

The instance role here is scoped to a single read-only action on a single named prefix, unlike the challenge role which could list an unrelated bucket (level6 bucket) it had no legitimate need to reach.
Validate with IAM Policy Simulator (console or aws iam simulate-custom-policy) confirming s3:ListBucket on any bucket other than the named prefix evaluates to implicitDeny.
